consensus_summary: Love is God-grounded, self-giving and faithful concern expressed in sacrificial action toward others and in devotion to God; it is the supreme Christian virtue and fulfills the law.
book_summary: Love is self-giving, faithful obedience to God’s law in every relationship, with obedience treated as a necessary condition of genuine love.
consensus_core_identification: Self-giving, faithful commitment to the good of God and neighbor, grounded in God’s own character and action.
book_core_identification: Self-giving, faithful conduct toward God and others specifically constituted and bounded by obedience to God’s law.
boundary_disagreement: The book excludes purportedly loving affection, benevolence, or even sacrificial action when it is disobedient to God’s commands. The consensus associates love closely with obedience and fulfillment of the law but does not uniformly make legal obedience the explicit defining boundary of every instance of love.
material_contradiction: There is no replacement of the consensus referent: both identify love as self-giving, faithful action toward God and others. The material difference is the book’s stronger necessary-condition claim that without obedience there is no love.
rationale: The entry retains the consensus category of active, self-giving faithfulness rather than proposing a different referent. Its distinctive move is to define that category more tightly through obedience to divine law. This is a substantive narrowing of extension, not a contradiction of the central consensus identification.
strongest_objection: The best case for MATCH is that the consensus already says love fulfills the law, entails covenant loyalty, and is inseparable from obedience and holiness. Nevertheless, the book’s categorical formulation—“without obedience, there is no love”—makes obedience an explicit exclusion criterion stronger than the broader consensus formulation.
